title: Hilbert--Samuel polynomial has degree equal to local Krull dimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. There exist a nonzero polynomial $Q_R(X)\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and an integer $N\ge1$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, the module $R/\mathfrak n^n$ has finite composition length [def-weil-pbc-module-length] and $\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak n^n)=Q_R(n)$. The leading coefficient of $Q_R$ is strictly positive, and its degree equals $\dim R$, the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial, applied to M=R and I=n, together with Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, equivalence (1) <=> (2); shifting chi(n)=length(R/n^(n+1)) to n does not change its degree.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n$ and $H_A(n)=\mathrm{length}_A(A/\mathfrak m_A^n)$ for any nonzero Noetherian local ring $A$. By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge], its maximal-adic graded algebra $S$ is standard over its residue field. Apply [lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function] to $M=S$, generated over itself by $1$ in degree zero. The resulting eventual polynomial for $\dim S_i$, followed by the bridge's last assertion, gives a nonzero $Q_A$ with positive leading coefficient and $H_A(n)=Q_A(n)$ eventually; all $H_A(n)$ for $n\ge1$ are finite. Put $e_A=\deg Q_A$.

source.place: Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial, associated graded construction and the preceding power-filtration identity; Tag 00JZ, lemma-numerical-polynomial, binomial-basis telescoping. Specialization I=m, M=R, and exponent n rather than n+1.

proof.text: For every proper ideal $I\subset R$, $R/I$ is nonzero, local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$, and Noetherian: its ideals correspond to ideals of $R$ containing $I$, whose finite generators descend. Thus step 1 supplies $Q_I=Q_{R/I}$ for every proper $I$, as required in [lem-trf-prime-chain-bound-from-colength-polynomials]. For prime $\mathfrak p$ and $x\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak p$, $A=R/\mathfrak p$ is a domain and $\bar x$ is a nonzero nonunit. Apply [lem-trf-artin-rees-principal-colength-difference] to $A,\bar x$; its finite-length hypotheses hold by step 1. The quotient is $R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$, and the power quotients and lengths agree under this identification. It supplies exactly the shifted-difference hypothesis of the prime-chain node. That node gives $\dim R\le e_R$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, last prime-chain paragraph: conditional polynomial-growth induction for all proper quotients, with the degree drop supplied as a shifted colength-difference hypothesis. Degree-zero base case and quotient-length comparison written explicitly in the repair report.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters], $d=\dim R$ is finite and there is $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ with $\mathfrak m^a\subseteq J$, $a\ge1$. The quotient $R/\mathfrak m^a\twoheadrightarrow R/J$ and [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] show $L=\mathrm{length}_R(R/J)<\infty$. By [lem-trf-parameter-ideal-colength-bound], if $d\ge1$ then $H_R(n)\le L\binom{n+d-1}{d}$, a degree-$d$ polynomial; if $d=0$ then $H_R(n)=L$ eventually. Since $Q_R$ has positive leading coefficient, either bound forces $e_R\le d$: a larger degree would eventually exceed that bound.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof of d-prime(R) >= d(R): degree-i monomial surjections and summation of power-quotient lengths. The d=0 nilpotent case is separated explicitly.

proof.text: The two bounds give $\deg Q_R=\dim R$. Step 1 supplies $Q_R\ne0$, its positive leading coefficient, all required finite lengths, and the eventual equality with exponent $n$. Take its threshold $N\ge1$. This proves the unchanged statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_hilbertSamuel_polynomial (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : ∃ Q : Polynomial ℚ, Q ≠ 0 ∧ 0 < Q.leadingCoeff ∧ (Q.natDegree : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → Module.length R (R ⧸ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n) < ⊤ ∧ ((Module.length R (R ⧸ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n)).toNat : ℚ) = Q.eval (n : ℚ)
